title: The duality pairing and the double-dual morphism
statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over a field, with finite
coefficients invertible on that field. On the ambient etale derived
category put $\omega_X=Ra_X^{\times}A$, using the right adjoint of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and let
$D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$. For every complex $K$, the
evaluation of internal Hom is a natural pairing

$$
\mathrm{ev}_K:D_XK\otimes_A^LK\longrightarrow\omega_X.
$$

Its transpose is the natural double-dual morphism
$\delta_K:K\to D_XD_XK$. It is compatible with shifts and is a
morphism of distinguished triangles. The same formal construction
applies on the pro-etale site whenever its ambient dualizing object is
specified; it does not assume that $D_XK$ is constructible.

proof.text: First work on any small ringed site $(\mathcal C,R)$ with a sheaf of commutative rings, and put $H(L,M)=R\mathcal Hom_R(L,M)$. The site may be chosen small in the universe of its module sheaves; on the pro-etale site this is the skeleton convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], $H(U,H(V,W))\cong H(U\otimes_R^L V,W)$ naturally. Apply $H^0(\mathcal C,-)$ and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] to obtain the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(U,H(V,W))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(U\otimes_R^L V,W)$. We also need tensor symmetry. On total tensor complexes it is $x_p\otimes y_q\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y_q\otimes x_p$: the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives the same coefficients $(-1)^{pq+q}$ and $(-1)^{pq}$ after interchanging the two differential summands, and the square of this map is the identity. By the resolving-class equivalence and natural-transformation descent of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], this natural chain isomorphism descends to $U\otimes_R^L V\cong V\otimes_R^L U$. Thus the adjunction and symmetry used below are available for arbitrary ambient objects on either site.

Fix an arbitrary $W\in D(R)$ and write $D=H(-,W)$. Under the bijection of step 1 the identity of $DK$ corresponds to $e_K:DK\otimes_R^L K\to W$. Define $\delta_K:K\to H(DK,W)=D^2K$ to correspond to $e_K\circ\sigma_{K,DK}:K\otimes_R^L DK\to W$. This is precisely the evaluation pairing followed by transposition, not an assertion that evaluation or $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism. For $u:K\to L$, naturality of the adjunction gives $e_K\circ(Du\otimes1_K)=e_L\circ(1_{DL}\otimes u)$ as maps $DL\otimes_R^L K\to W$. Transpose this equality after tensor symmetry; it becomes $D^2u\circ\delta_K=\delta_L\circ u$. This proves the asserted naturality (the displayed identity is the precise variance convention for naturality of evaluation). Both uses of adjunction take place in the ambient derived category, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections].

source.place: Tag 08J9 and equation (equation-internal-hom); evaluation as the adjunct of the identity

proof.text: Here is a representative calculation that will check the shift assertion. Choose a K-injective complex $I$ representing $W$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Write $T(C)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(C,I)$, using [def-pur-hom-complex]. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $T(C)$ represents $DC$ and $T(T(C))$ represents $D^2C$; the second assertion only requires that the second variable $I$ be K-injective, not that $T(C)$ be K-injective. These assignments invert quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]. On homogeneous local sections $x\in C^p$, $f\in T(C)^q$, define $b_C(x)(f)=(-1)^{pq}f(x)$. The Hom differential gives $(d b_C(x))(f)=(-1)^{pq}d_I(f(x))-(-1)^{pq}(d_I(f(x))-(-1)^qf(d_Cx))=(-1)^{(p+1)q}f(d_Cx)=b_C(d_Cx)(f)$; hence $b_C:C\to T^2C$ is a chain map, natural for chain maps. To identify its localization with the transpose in step 2, take K-flat resolutions $P\to C$ and $r:Q\to T(P)$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $Q\otimes P$ computes $DP\otimes_R^L P$, now with both tensor factors K-flat. By [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], both $T(P)$ and $T(Q)$ are K-injective. Thus the derived currying of step 1 is computed by ordinary Hom-complex currying on these representatives. That currying sends $g$ to the map $x\otimes q\mapsto g(x)(q)$: substituting the Hom and tensor differentials gives $d_Ig(x)(q)-(-1)^n g(d_Px)(q)-(-1)^{n+p}g(x)(d_Qq)$ on both sides for a degree-$n$ map $g$ and $x\in P^p$. Under the morphism-set adjunction, the identity of $DP$ is represented by $r:Q\to T(P)$, so evaluation on $Q\otimes P$ is $q\otimes x\mapsto r(q)(x)$. Symmetry followed by evaluation is $x\otimes q\mapsto(-1)^{p\deg(q)}r(q)(x)$. Currying the latter gives $T(r)\circ b_P:P\to T(Q)$. The map $T(r):T^2(P)\to T(Q)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], so this is exactly $b_P$ after the canonical derived identification. Naturality and the same quasi-isomorphism theorem identify the localization of $b_C$ with $\delta_C$.

We make the double-dual shift comparison explicit. With cochain shifts as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a chain isomorphism $s_{C,m}:T(C[m])\to T(C)[-m]$ sending a degree-$q$ map $f$ to $(-1)^{mq}f$, after reindexing its components. Substitution into $d(f)=d_If-(-1)^qfd_C$ checks it is a chain map. Put $\chi_C=-s_{T(C),-1}\circ T(s_{C,1})^{-1}:T^2(C[1])\to T^2(C)[1]$. Concretely, on a degree-$p$ map $g\in T^2(C[1])^p$ and $y\in T(C)^r$, this is $(\chi_Cg)(y)=(-1)^{p+r}g(y)$, where the argument on the right is reindexed into $T(C[1])^{r+1}$. We check directly that this is an exact comparison, rather than deducing the sign from exactness alone. For a chain map $u:A\to B$, let $E=\operatorname{Cone}(u)$, with maps $i:B\to E$ and $\pi:E\to A[1]$; its cone triangle ends in $-\pi$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $X=T(B)$, $Y=T(A)$, and $h=T(u)$. A degree-$q$ element of $T(E)$ is $(x,y)\in X^q\oplus Y^{q-1}$, and [def-pur-hom-complex] gives differential $(d_Xx,d_Yy+(-1)^{q+1}h(x))$. Write a degree-$p$ element of $T^2(E)$ as $(\alpha,\beta)$, where $\alpha:X^q\to I^{q+p}$ and $\beta:Y^r\to I^{r+p+1}$. Set $\gamma(y)=(-1)^{p+r}\beta(y)$ for $y\in Y^r$. Then $\theta_E(\alpha,\beta)=(\alpha,\gamma)$ identifies $T^2(E)$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(T^2u)$. Indeed, the first differential component on $x\in X^q$ is $d_{T^2B}\alpha(x)+(-1)^{p+q}\beta(h(x))=d_{T^2B}\alpha(x)+(T^2u)(\gamma)(x)$, and the second raw component is $\beta'(y)=d_I\beta(y)-(-1)^p\beta(d_Yy)$; multiplying it by $(-1)^{p+1+r}$ gives $\gamma'=-d_{T^2A}\gamma$. These are exactly the cone differential components. Under $\theta_E$, $T^2(i)$ is inclusion into the first component. Also $T^2(\pi)$ is the raw second component $\beta$, so $\chi_A\circ T^2(-\pi)=-\operatorname{pr}_2\circ\theta_E$, exactly the connecting map of the cone of $T^2u$. Hence $T^2$, with $\chi$, sends each cone triangle to a cone triangle; localization and invariance under triangle isomorphisms give the assertion for all distinguished triangles. This makes the shift sign in the exactness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] explicit. Finally, for $x\in C[1]^p=C^{p+1}$ and $\psi\in T(C)^t$, the three signs in $\chi_C b_{C[1]}(x)(\psi)$ have exponent $1+p+p(t+1)+(t+1)\equiv(p+1)t\pmod2$. Therefore $\chi_C\circ b_{C[1]}=b_C[1]$. Localization gives $\chi_K\circ\delta_{K[1]}=\delta_K[1]$. Iterating this identity and its inverse gives compatibility with every integer shift.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism] to $F_1=\mathrm{id}$, $F_2=D^2$, and $\tau=\delta$. Naturality is step 2, and the required equation with the shift comparisons is step 4. Hence for every distinguished triangle $K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$, the three components $(\delta_{K'},\delta_K,\delta_{K''})$ form a morphism to its $D^2$-image triangle, which is distinguished by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and the exact comparison checked in step 4. This supplies in particular the last square involving the connecting arrow; it is not inferred merely from exactness of the two functors.

source.place: Tag 08JC; for the formal triangle-morphism step, literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, Definitions 0144 and 014V

proof.text: Specialize the preceding argument to the small etale ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_X)$ and $W=\omega_X$ already specified in the statement using [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. This gives exactly $e_K:\!D_XK\otimes_A^LK\to\omega_X$ and its transpose $\delta_K$ with all the asserted compatibilities. Instantiate steps 1–5 instead with $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $R=A_X$, and the specified ambient object $W=\omega_X$: step 2 gives its evaluation and double-dual arrow, step 4 gives the shift equation, and step 5 gives the triangle morphism. This proves the pro-etale clause. The arguments above used arbitrary objects of $D(R)$ throughout; no assertion about $D_XK$ being constructible, and no comparison equivalence between the two sites, is used.
